findings.title: require_admin always rejects everyone
findings.description: The condition `session.role != "admin" || session.role != "owner"` is true for every possible role, so the function returns false even for admins/owners. No request can ever pass the admin check.

findings.title: verify does not enforce session expiry
findings.description: verify returns a pointer to the session without checking expires_at, despite its contract that an expired token yields nullptr. Expired tokens remain usable indefinitely.

findings.title: bearer_token overflows fixed buffer and dereferences possibly-null strchr result
findings.description: header is copied into char[64] with std::strcpy, so any Authorization header of 64+ bytes overflows the stack buffer. std::strchr may return nullptr when there is no space, and `space + 1` then dereferences null.

findings.title: Cache leaks heap-allocated Entry objects
findings.description: Entries are allocated with `new Entry()` and stored as raw pointers. The destructor only clears the map (leaking every Entry), and get/erase/sweep/eviction/overwrite paths discard pointers without deleting them.

findings.title: sweep erases during iteration, invalidating iterators
findings.description: The loop increments `it` and then calls entries_.erase(it) on expiry, which is undefined behavior and can skip/corrupt entries or crash.

findings.title: utilization integer division always reports 0 until full
findings.description: entries_.size() (size_t) / limit_ (size_t) is integer division, so the percentage is 0 unless the cache is completely full.

findings.title: LINKD_TIMEOUT_MS and LINKD_CACHE_TTL_MS are treated as seconds, not milliseconds
findings.description: The comment and names say milliseconds, but the values are assigned directly to Seconds, so a 10000 ms timeout becomes 10000 seconds. The bad-value guard also assigns Seconds{0} anyway.

findings.title: LINKD_FETCH_LIMIT is parsed but never applied
findings.description: parsed is computed and then discarded with (void)parsed, so cfg.fetch_limit keeps its default regardless of the environment.

findings.title: validate() returns true even when problems are found
findings.description: Although problems are collected and printed, the function unconditionally returns true, so invalid configurations pass startup validation.

findings.title: format_row returns dangling pointer to stack buffer
findings.description: row is a local char[128] stack array, and returning it as const char* yields a dangling pointer once the function returns.

findings.title: resolve has inverted expiry condition and uses an erased iterator
findings.description: It erases the link when `now < expires_at` (i.e. while still valid) and then accesses the erased iterator to increment hits, which is undefined behavior. Expired links are instead resolved.

findings.title: rename validates `from` twice instead of validating `to`
findings.description: validate_code(from) is called twice and the new code `to` is never validated, allowing invalid renamed codes.

findings.title: page() clamps end to size()+1, reading past the vector end
findings.description: When end exceeds size it is set to all.size()+1, producing an out-of-range constructor range and undefined behavior.

findings.title: success_rate integer division truncates to 0 unless all links are used
findings.description: used / links_.size() is computed before multiplying by 100, so any partial adoption reports 0%.

findings.title: remove() does not return the owner's quota slot
findings.description: quota_ is never decremented on deletion, contradicting the documented behavior that a deleted link frees the owner's slot.

findings.title: top() sorts ascending and resizes without guarding n > size
findings.description: Links are sorted least-first (a.hits < b.hits) so the leaderboard is backwards. resize(n) also value-initializes extra Links when n exceeds the vector size.

findings.title: by_owner() matches substrings instead of exact owners
findings.description: pair.second.owner.find(owner) != npos returns links for any owner containing the query, not links belonging to exactly that owner.

findings.title: extend() revives expired links despite contract
findings.description: expiry is unconditionally set to now+ttl even for already-expired links, contradicting the documented finality of expiry.

findings.title: quotas() returns a mutable reference to internal state
findings.description: The documented snapshot semantics are violated: callers can mutate the store's quota_ directly through the returned reference.

findings.title: import_all is not atomic and partially commits on failure
findings.description: Links are inserted as the loop runs; a later validate_code failure (or duplicate handling) leaves earlier entries in the store, violating the all-or-none contract.

findings.title: prune() erases during iteration and returns the wrong value
findings.description: Erasing `it` without advancing is undefined behavior, and the function returns links_.size() instead of the number removed as documented.

findings.title: last_code() returns a dangling view and is not the newest
findings.description: It returns a string_view into a local std::string that is destroyed on return. It also reports the lexicographically last key rather than the most recently created code (no ordering/recording).

findings.title: janitor erases from the store map while iterating it
findings.description: store.all().erase(it) invalidates the iterator and the for-loop then increments it; undefined behavior. Also sleep occurs before sweeping.

findings.title: warm_cache spawns joinable threads but never joins them
findings.description: workers threads are destroyed while still running (std::terminate/UB), and the loop-captured `link` reference may dangle before the threads read it.

findings.title: check_targets reads one past the end of links
findings.description: The loop condition `i <= links.size()` accesses links[links.size()], out of bounds.

findings.title: stats() divides by zero when the store is empty
findings.description: total_hits() / g_store->size() is computed unconditionally, crashing when no links exist.

findings.title: Metrics::errors_ is uninitialized
findings.description: resolved_ and created_ have default member initializers but errors_ does not, so reading errors() (used in stats()) returns indeterminate value.

findings.title: Authenticator::sessions_ map is accessed without synchronization
findings.description: issue(), verify(), and revoke() all read and mutate the shared sessions_ map from request threads with no mutex or atomic protection. verify() also returns a pointer into that map, which can be invalidated by a concurrent issue() insertion or revoke() erasure, leading to a data race and use-after-free. An interleaving of verify() on one thread and revoke() on another returns a dangling Session*.

findings.title: Cache shared state (entries_ and hits_) is accessed without synchronization
findings.description: get(), peek(), set(), erase(), and sweep() all touch entries_ and hits_ with no lock. The janitor thread calls sweep() while request threads call get()/set(), and warm_cache spawns threads calling set(), so concurrent operations race on the std::map and on the hits_ counter, with potential corruption or crashes.

findings.title: Store maps links_ and quota_ are mutated without synchronization
findings.description: Every Store method reads or writes links_ and quota_ with no mutex, while multiple request threads and the janitor thread operate concurrently. Interleaved create/resolve/remove/import_all/prune can corrupt the maps or invalidate iterators and pointers, and create() returns a pointer into links_ that another thread may erase.

findings.title: Store::quotas() exposes the internal map by reference
findings.description: quotas() returns a mutable reference to the live quota_ map, defeating the documented snapshot semantics. Callers such as admin_quotas and count_for_owner read or insert entries while concurrent create/remove mutate quota_, producing data races.

findings.title: Store::all() leaks a mutable reference to the internal links_ map
findings.description: all() returns links_ by non-const reference, allowing the janitor to iterate and erase entries directly while request threads access the same map through other methods, causing unsynchronized concurrent mutation.

findings.title: Janitor thread operates on store/cache without synchronization
findings.description: start_janitor spawns a thread that loops erasing entries via store.all() and calling cache.sweep() with no lock, racing with every request-thread operation. Its erase-while-iterating loop also increments an iterator after erasing the current element, which is undefined behavior and can corrupt the map.

findings.title: stop_janitor never joins the janitor thread
findings.description: stop_janitor only flips g_running; it never calls join() on g_janitor. On shutdown the thread can keep executing against a Store/Cache that is being destroyed, a use-after-free, and the raw thread* is leaked.

findings.title: warm_cache launches threads it never joins and captures a dangling loop reference
findings.description: Each lambda captures &link referring to the range-based loop variable, which is reused across iterations, so threads may read a dangling/stale reference. The workers vector is destroyed without joining its threads, which calls std::terminate. cache.set() also races on shared state.

findings.title: Metrics counters are incremented non-atomically from multiple request threads
findings.description: add_resolved() and add_created() perform resolved_++/created_++ without synchronization or atomics, and resolved()/created() read them concurrently, so concurrent requests race and can lose updates or read torn values.
